extracted.intended_audience: parties, potential parties, interested governmental participants, attorneys, and Licensing Support Network (LSN) participants and administrators in NRC high-level radioactive waste (HLW) licensing proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards and procedural requirements governing electronic submissions, Licensing Support Network (LSN) operation, discovery, depositions, filing/appeals, computation of time, and prehearing conferences in NRC high-level radioactive waste (HLW) licensing proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliographic header data format
rubrics_metrics.description: Structured bibliographic header data must be made available in a database-readable format (e.g., ANSI/ISO-compliant DBMS) or in standard database-readable files such as XML or comma-delimited (.csv).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Header data may be stored in a compliant DBMS (ANSI X3.135-1992/ISO 9075-1992) or provided as XML, CSV, or similar. Participants shall programmatically link the bibliographic header record with the text or image file it represents (preferably via hyperlink or other automated process) so the LSN software can identify files to their bibliographic data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Textual material encoding and acceptable formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Textual material must comply with ISO/IEC 8859-1 character set and be submitted in an acceptable format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable formats include ASCII, native word processing (Word, WordPerfect), PDF Normal, or HTML.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image file formats and image quality standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Image files must be formatted as TIFF CCITT G4 for bi-tonal images, PNG for gray-scale or color images, or PDF (image). Images will be stored at specified minimum resolutions and color depths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TIFF/PDF/PNG images stored at 300 dpi or greater for bi-tonal; gray scale images at 150 dpi or greater with 8 bits tonal depth; color images at 150 dpi or greater with 24 bits color depth. Images on participant machines stored as single image-per-page to facilitate retrieval unless server software allows image-per-page representation from image-per-document format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programmatic linking of metadata to content
rubrics_metrics.description: Each participant must programmatically link bibliographic header records with the text or image files they describe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Linking should preferably be via hyperlink or an automated process. Each participant's system must provide enough information to allow LSN software to identify a text or image file to its bibliographic data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Network and protocol standards for data exchange
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants shall adhere to specific hardware and software network standards to facilitate data exchange.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements include: network access via HTTP/1.1 over TCP over IP; DNS per RFC1034/1035; web pages constructed in HTML; e-mail exchange via SMTP; e-mail message format per RFC822 optionally extended by MIME (RFC2045) to accommodate multipurpose mail.

rubrics_metrics.name: LSN Administrator responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The LSN Administrator shall coordinate the Licensing Support Network and perform specified technical, policy, and operational duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responsibilities include: identifying technical and policy issues for Advisory Review Panel and Commission consideration; addressing Advisory Panel consensus consistent with subpart requirements; identifying LSN availability problems and recommending resolutions; identifying integrity problems with certified documentary material and recommending resolutions; providing periodic reports on LSN functionality/operability; evaluating participant compliance with basic design standards and providing for variances; and issuing guidance to participants on complying with design standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: LSN Advisory Review Panel duties and composition
rubrics_metrics.description: An LSN Advisory Review Panel shall advise the NRC, the Secretary, and the LSN Administrator on LSN functioning and electronic docket operation and provide advice on standards and procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel composition follows prior LSS Advisory Review Panel interests; Secretary may appoint additional representatives consistent with the Federal Advisory Committee Act. Panel responsibilities include advice on format standards for electronic access to certified documentary material, procedures/standards for electronic transmission of filings/orders/decisions, and other duties specified in the subpart or by the Secretary.

rubrics_metrics.name: DOE certification and docketing timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Department of Energy (DOE) fails to make initial certification at least six months prior to tendering the application, the NRC will delay docketing until six months after certification; the Director may deem the tendered application unacceptable for docketing under certain conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director may find application unacceptable if not accompanied by updated certification under § 2.1009(b), or if Secretary finds application not submitted on optical storage media in a format consistent with NRC regulations/guidance, or for non-compliance with other subpart requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Party status conditioned on substantial and timely compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: A person (including potential parties given LSN access) may not be granted party status under § 2.309 or interested governmental participant status under § 2.315 unless it can demonstrate substantial and timely compliance with § 2.1003 at the time of requesting participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A person denied status for non-compliance may request status upon showing subsequent compliance; admission is conditioned on accepting the status of the proceeding at the time of admission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presiding Officer compliance requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Presiding Officer shall not find a person in substantial and timely compliance if that person is not in compliance with all applicable orders of the Pre-License Application Presiding Officer designated under § 2.1010.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic docket official record and format
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary will maintain the official docket and establish an electronic docket to contain the official record materials of the HLW licensing proceeding in searchable full text or by header and image when not suitable for full text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic docket is the official record for the proceeding under parts 60 or 63.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibits availability before hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Absent good cause, all exhibits to be tendered during hearings must have been made available electronically to the parties before the portion of the hearing in which the exhibit will be offered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The electronic docket must contain a list of all exhibits showing where marked in the transcript and whether received into evidence or rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transcript and video transcript entry timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Transcripts of stenographically recorded hearing sessions will be entered into the electronic docket on a daily basis; transcripts prepared from video recordings will be entered within 24 hours of the time the transcript is tendered to the electronic docket by the transcription service if daily video copies afford next-day availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic transmission categories and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Filings must be transmitted according to categories: 'simple documents', 'large documents', and 'complex documents', with specific electronic transmission requirements and use of optical storage media where necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Simple documents' via EIE; 'Large documents' in multiple transmissions of 50 MB or less via EIE; 'Complex documents'—portions capable of electronic submission in 50 MB or less via EIE with transmittal letter, portions not capable submitted on optical storage media (which must also include portions transmitted electronically).

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic submission resolution standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronic submissions created after Jan 1, 2004 must meet minimum resolution standards; older files or files that cannot meet 300 dpi have defined alternate standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After Jan 1, 2004: 300 dpi minimum for bi-tonal, color, and grayscale except limited circumstances. Files created before Jan 1, 2004 or files after that date that cannot meet 300 dpi must meet § 2.1011(b)(2)(iv) standards: 150 dpi for color/grayscale and 300 dpi for bi-tonal.

rubrics_metrics.name: PDF generation and conversion requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronic submissions must be generated in appropriate PDF output formats depending on document type; TIFF images and spreadsheet outputs should be converted to PDF when practicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PDF—Formatted Text and Graphics for textual documents converted from native apps; PDF—Searchable Image (Exact) for scanned textual documents; PDF—Image Only for graphic-, image-, and forms-oriented documents. TIFF images, spreadsheet results, etc., must be converted to PDF except where impracticable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on reliance upon external hyperlinks
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronic submissions must not rely on hyperlinks to other documents or websites for completeness or access, except hyperlinks linking to material within the same PDF file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If hyperlinks to other documents or websites are included, the submittal must include a disclaimer that hyperlinks may be inoperable or not essential; information necessary for completeness that is contained only in hyperlinks must be submitted in its entirety in the filing or as an attachment.

rubrics_metrics.name: No author-imposed security restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: All electronic submissions must be free of author-imposed security restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service completion and proof of service for electronic filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Service upon a party is completed when the sender receives electronic acknowledgment (delivery receipt). Proof of service must be shown for each filed document by acceptable methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable proof: electronic acknowledgment (delivery receipt), affidavit of the person making service, or certificate of counsel. When a party has appeared by attorney, service must be upon the attorney of record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmission of Presiding Officer and Commission issuances
rubrics_metrics.description: All Presiding Officer and Commission issuances and orders will be transmitted electronically to the parties and interested governmental participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online docket access during hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: Online access to the electronic docket (including Protective Order File if authorized) shall be provided to the Presiding Officer, representatives of parties and interested governmental participants, and witnesses while testifying, for use during the hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of paper copies and other images is also permitted at the hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal timing and filing requirements (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: No appeals from Pre-License Application Presiding Officer or Presiding Officer orders are permitted except as prescribed; specified types of notices of appeal must be filed within set timeframes and accompanied by supporting briefs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice of appeal for certain presiding officer orders must be filed with the Commission no later than 10 days after service of the order and must include a supporting brief. Other parties may file opposition briefs within 10 days after service of the appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals from initial decisions: notice and briefing schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals from a Presiding Officer initial decision must follow specified notice and briefing timelines and content requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice of appeal within 10 days after service of an initial decision. Appellants file briefs supporting position within 30 days (40 days if Commission staff is appellant). Responsive briefs due within 30 days after appellant briefs (staff 40 days). A responding party files a single responsive brief regardless of number of appellants' briefs filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief content and length rules on appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Briefs in excess of 10 pages must include a table of contents and a table of cases/statutes; appellant's brief must identify errors of fact or law and precise record portions; responsive briefs must reference precise record portions; page limit and extension process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Briefs over 10 pages must contain TOC with page references and table of cases/statutes/authorities with page references. Appellant must clearly identify errors and record portions supporting each assertion. A party shall not file a brief longer than 70 pages (exclusive of TOC, table of citations, addendum); requests for enlargement must be made for good cause at least 7 days before due date and specify enlargement requested. All documents must have a certificate of service. Noncompliant briefs may be stricken.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of appeal on proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing an appeal, petition for review, referral, or request for certification of a ruling does not stay the proceeding or extend time for performance of acts unless otherwise ordered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presiding Officer may refer rulings to Commission for prompt appellate review if necessary to prevent detriment to the public interest or unusual delay/expense; parties may request certification under § 2.319.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of time rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for computing time periods: exclude day of act, include last day unless weekend/holiday, add one day when time runs after service, and treatment when electronic docket unavailable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the last day is Saturday, Sunday, or legal holiday at the place where the action/event is to occur, period runs until end of next day that is not such. Whenever a party has a right to act within a period after service, one day shall be added. If the electronic docket is unavailable for more than four access hours of any day that would be counted, that day will not be counted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery methods allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties, potential parties, and interested governmental participants may obtain discovery by specified methods including access to documentary material made available pursuant to § 2.1003, entry upon land, production of copies of bibliographic-header-only material, depositions (oral and written), requests for admissions, informal requests for information, and interrogatories/written questions as authorized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interrogatories and depositions upon written questions may be authorized by order of the discovery master or Presiding Officer if parties cannot resolve disputes after good faith efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: Discovery may cover any non-privileged matter relevant to the licensing of the likely candidate site for a geologic repository, whether related to the claim/defense of the party seeking discovery or another party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Except for certain provisions, discovery begins during pre-license application phase; discovery is not objectionable merely because information sought may be inadmissible at hearing if it appears reasonably calculated to lead to admissible evidence. Some discovery (interrogatories and written depositions) begins after issuance of the first pre-hearing conference order and is limited to issues defined in that order or subsequent amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work-product and trial-preparation protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents prepared in anticipation of hearing or for another party's representative are discoverable only upon a showing of substantial need and inability to obtain equivalent without undue hardship, with protection for attorney mental impressions/opinions/theories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When discovery ordered under this showing, the Presiding Officer shall protect against disclosure of mental impressions, conclusions, opinions, or legal theories of an attorney or other representative concerning the proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protective orders and limitations on discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon motion and for good cause, the Presiding Officer may issue protective orders to protect parties/others from annoyance, embarrassment, oppression, undue burden, delay, or expense, including specific restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Possible orders include: that discovery not be had; limited time/place/manner; alternative discovery methods; limited scope; conduct with only designated persons present; restrictions on disclosure of trade secrets or confidential information (subject to § 2.390); or that studies/evaluations not be prepared. If protective order denied, the Presiding Officer may order discovery on just terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequencing and non-delay of discovery methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless Presiding Officer orders otherwise for convenience or interest of justice, discovery methods may be used in any sequence, and one party's use of discovery does not delay others' discovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to supplement discovery responses
rubrics_metrics.description: A party who made available material electronically or responded completely when made is generally under no duty to supplement except in specified circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obligations to supplement include: seasonably supplementing interrogatory answers that inquire about identity/location of persons with knowledge and identity/subject matter/substance of expert witnesses; amending prior responses that were incorrect when made or are no longer true such that failure to amend would be knowing concealment. Presiding Officer may impose duty to supplement by order or parties may agree.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to compel responses and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: If a deponent fails to respond or objects, the requesting party may move the Presiding Officer within five days after response or failure to respond for an order compelling a response; evasive/incomplete answers treated as failures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Motion must set forth nature of questions/requests, the response/objection, and arguments. Failure to answer not excused because discovery is objectionable unless the person applied for a protective order. In ruling, Presiding Officer may make protective orders authorized under discovery protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent subpoenas to nonparties and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: An independent request for issuance of a subpoena may be directed to a nonparty for production of documents; certain rules (e.g., requests for NRC regulatory staff testimony under § 2.709) are exempt from this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery master appointment
rubrics_metrics.description: The Presiding Officer may appoint a discovery master to resolve disputes between parties concerning informal requests for information as provided in discovery provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discovery master appointments are under § 2.322 authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depositions notice and procedural rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for taking depositions by oral examination: reasonable written notice to all parties, deponent, and Presiding Officer with details; depositions may be taken before authorized officers domestically or certain consular/embassy officials abroad; telephone/video depositions allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice must include proposed time/place, name/address of each person to be examined (or descriptive identification), matters to be examined, and officer before whom deposition taken. Deponent sworn/affirmed; examination proceeds as at hearing; questions recorded; evidence subject to objection; objections noted in short form. Transcription, certification, signature procedures specified, with electronic copy transmitted to Secretary for docket.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depositions on written questions procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: When depositions are taken on written questions, serve questions showing each question separately and consecutively numbered on every other party with notice of person to answer and officer; other parties may serve cross-questions within ten days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions, cross-questions, and answers recorded, signed, certified, returned, and transmitted in electronic form to Secretary for docket similar to oral deposition procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depositions and evidentiary record
rubrics_metrics.description: A deposition does not become part of the evidentiary record unless received in evidence; if only part is offered, other parties may introduce other parts. Taking deposition does not make the person the depositor's witness for any purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees and counsel attendance for depositions
rubrics_metrics.description: Deponent and officer are entitled to fees as in U.S. district courts, paid by the taking party; deponent may be accompanied, represented, and advised by counsel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-deposition electronic index and document production
rubrics_metrics.description: Ten days before deposition, the deponent must submit an electronic index of all documents in their possession relevant to the deposition subject matter, identifying records already made available electronically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index should include specified categories; documents not identical to those already made available electronically (e.g., modified or with added notations) treated as separate documents. Certain materials are excluded from initial electronic availability requirements (personal records, travel vouchers, speeches, preliminary drafts, marginalia) but are subject to derivative discovery. Parties may request paper copies of documents not already provided electronically; deponent shall bring paper copies of requested documents to oral deposition or submit with certified deposition when deposition on written questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry upon land request and response requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Any party may serve a request for entry upon designated land/property for inspection, raw data access, measuring, surveying, photographing, testing, or sampling within the scope of discovery; request may be served without leave.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request must describe the land/property with reasonable particularity by item or category and specify reasonable time/place/manner. The recipient must respond in writing within 10 days stating whether inspection/activities will be permitted as requested or state specific objections and reasons; if objection to part, specify the part.

rubrics_metrics.name: First prehearing conference purposes and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: In HLW repository licensing proceedings under parts 60 or 63, the Commission or presiding officer will direct parties and interested persons to appear at a first prehearing conference within 70 days after notice of hearing (or at other appropriate time) to accomplish specified objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conference objectives include: permit identification of key issues; take steps for further identification of issues; consider intervention petitions to allow determinations of parties/participants; establish schedule for further actions; and establish a discovery schedule considering the objective of meeting the 3-year schedule in Section 114(d) of the Nuclear Waste Policy Act.
